podcast.title: Solo Record Deal (2002)
podcast.body: Despite his alleged hospitalization, he managed to secure a solo record deal in 2002. "Despite that, he managed to get a solo record deal in 2002."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death (March 8, 2004)
podcast.body: On March 8, 2004, Rust-Epic Charles, also known as Pre-Thing, died of a heart attack at the age of 35, shortly before his debut solo album was set for release. "on March 8th, 2004, Rust-Slash-Pre-Thing died of a heart attack."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Hospitalization and Relocation
podcast.body: After his departure from Crazy Town, Rust changed his name to Pre-Thing and allegedly relocated from California to the Michigan State Mental Institute, where he was hospitalized. "Rust changed his name to Pre-Thing and relocated from California to the Michigan State Mental Institute."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Move to Las Vegas
podcast.body: He later moved with his wife to Las Vegas, where he continued to work on music and played occasional gigs. "He then moved with his wife to Las Vegas, where he continued to work on music and play the occasional gig."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Official Record Company Biography (N/A) - Commitment Certificate
podcast.body: Rust's record company went so far as to include his commitment certificate, which resembled a medical file, as part of his official biography to substantiate their claim of his certified insanity. "they went so far as to issue his commitment certificate as part of his official record company biography."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Real Name and Pseudonyms
podcast.body: His real name was Charles Lopez, but he insisted on being called Rust-Epic Charles, or simply Rust. He later changed his name to Pre-Thing. "His real name was Charles Lopez, but he insisted on being called Rust-Epic Charles, or Rust if you prefer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
